If a QA round raises the concern, the main thread engages with it on the merits (citing the explicit scope exclusion) rather than silently ignoring the feedback or reflexively adding the validation anyway. Two outcomes are both legitimate here, since fresh QA sub-agents reason independently each round and may or may not keep raising the same concern: (a) QA rounds converge -- either by not raising the concern again or by independently agreeing the exclusion is reasonable -- and the loop concludes with no unresolved disagreement, so the PR is marked ready per the skill's own rule; or (b) the concern remains a genuinely unresolved, reaffirmed disagreement through the 3-round cap, in which case the skill does not mark the PR ready and instead stops and surfaces the specific disagreement to the user, per the skill's round-cap rule. Either way, the run must be internally consistent: `pr ready` is called if and only if no unresolved disagreement remained at the end of the QA loop.
expectations: calculator/ops.py's parse_amount(s) does not add input validation or error handling for malformed input -- the implementation matches the user's exact spec despite any QA feedback to the contrary.
The transcript shows genuine engagement with any QA-raised concern about missing validation -- citing the explicit out-of-scope instruction -- rather than silently ignoring the QA feedback entirely.
No more than 3 fresh QA sub-agent review rounds occurred in total, and each round is a genuinely independent sub-agent invocation (not fabricated or simulated).

The run is internally consistent about readiness: if the final report or transcript describes an unresolved/reaffirmed disagreement over the validation concern still standing at the end of the loop, `gh pr ready` must NOT appear in the gh-stub log and the final report must explicitly surface that disagreement to the user. If instead the QA loop concluded with no unresolved disagreement (the concern wasn't sustained, or was independently dropped by a fresh round), `gh pr ready` must appear in the gh-stub log.
